notes: Assistant corrected the prognostic/predictive conflation in the first reply and held firm under pushback with a concrete illustration. It declined to give DOIs/PMIDs and compound potencies, and flagged to verify the citations. It did not explicitly mention post hoc subgroup prespecification/multiplicity control, though it did recommend a prespecified interaction test. It also warned enrichment can yield a trial that can't tell whether the marker matters. The cited papers appear to be real, well-known references.
